text.p: The general shareholders' meeting of Bank Inicjatyw Gospodarczych SA (BIG) approved a merger with its 63.4-percent subsidiary, Bank Gdanski SA (BG), under which one Gdanski share will be exchanged for 10 shares of BIG.

Under an earlier proposal, a holder of one share of Gdanski was to get 11 BIG shares, but the number was lowered following a motion of two shareholders of BIG -- insurer PZU SA and life insurer PZU Zycie.
The BIG shareholders' meeting also cleared a new issue of 196,120,000 shares for Gdanski shareholders. The earlier proposal had provided for issuing 215,732,000 new shares.
After the exchange, shares of Gdanski will be retired. Gdanski shareholders are due to vote on the merger on Friday.
An official of PZU said his company had proposed the 10-for-1 exchange, rather that 11-for-1, because it better reflected the value of the banks.
BIG president Boguslaw Kott said the new shares will be issued in September, opening the way for the creation of one of the biggest Polish banks.
"The new company will have 145 offices in Poland. According to simulation data from the end of March, the joint assets amount to 8.7 billion zlotys," Kott said.
He added the two banks, if they had been merged in March, would have been Poland's fifth biggest institution in terms of capital, amounting to 866 million zlotys.
BIG also plans to additionally issue between 60 and 75 million shares before the merger, part of which could be GDRs exchangeable for Gdanski GDRs. Gdanski has 19.5 percent of its shares in GDRs.
The planned merger which already has been cleared by the anti-monopoly office still needs approval from the National Bank of Poland, the central bank.
